# Charlotte Latin School — International Travel — Deep Research

**⚠️ This is an AI-generated research summary, not a primary source.** The PDF was
produced by Claude deep research. Treat every claim below as a **lead to verify**, not as
evidence. A fact may reach the app only once it has been confirmed on a live page, normally
the school's own site, and that page's URL has been recorded in the companion
`Charlotte Latin - International Travel - Source URLs.md`. A claim that cannot be
confirmed stays here as research history and renders nowhere.

Travel & Global Education Programs — Research Dossier (as of October 2026)"*, a 23-page
deep-research PDF (filename `Charlotte Latin School Global Travel and Global Education
Programs_ 2026 Research Dossier.pdf`) the user supplied while running `/global-exposure`.
It was written from the `/global-exposure` prompt template (v2), sections 1–20. Every URL
below is copied from the PDF; the Source URLs file records which were re-checked and what
they actually say.

Source-type tags are copied from the PDF: **[Official]** = charlottelatin.org pages, news
posts, PDFs and the school's Google Site; **[Secondary]** = third-party.

**Student names.** The PDF names one student (a 2016 Harvard MUN commendation); this file
does not. The school's own pages name students, parents and trip leaders; the app names
none of them.

**Costs and exact travel dates.** Recorded here per the data-provenance standard. They are
**not rendered** on the page (privacy rule).

**Planning notes on the PDF's accuracy** (found at verification, 2026-10-13):
- **The PDF's biggest gap is the Google Site.** It reports the Global Studies Google Site
 (`https://sites.google.com/charlottelatin.org/globalstudies`) as blocked by a tool
 permission. It loads with plain `curl`, and it holds the 2026–27 program list with dates,
 maximum enrollment, prices, homestays, eligibility, selection, the full sign-up calendar
 and a safety FAQ (International SOS). The PDF's "NOT PUBLISHED" verdicts on trip prices,
 dates, deadlines, selection, vendor and safety are therefore **wrong**: all are published
 there. Its §11 questions 2–7 are largely answered.
- **"Global Studies and Travel Opportunities" (`/leading-programs/global-studies-and-travel-opportunities`)
 now returns 404.** Its content survives in a Wayback copy of 2025-10-22. The PDF quoted it
 as live.
- **The PDF says "No announced upcoming trips found."** Eight 2026–27 programs are
 announced on the Google Site.
- **"School years 2021–22 through 2025–26 … no specific dated student trips."** Wrong: the
 school's "Charlotte Latin Goes Global" post (summer 2025) names seven destination
 countries; a 2023 Argentina trip blog and a 2023 England (ISCA) trip-leader quote exist;
 a 2026 South Africa course blog exists; and an October 2025 Wayback copy names the
 2025–26 Upper School programs.
- **"Global Partners appears in the TK and KG social studies lists"** and **Grade 2
 "Schools Around the World"** were not found on the live Lower School page (it has
 "Holidays Around The World"). The Global Education page does list the Lower School
 Global Partners and Passport programs.
- **Upper School course electives** "H Edible Culture and Conflict", "H Human Rights",
 "Postcolonial Literature" come from the 2020–21 profile and are not on the live Course
 Offerings page.

Charlotte Latin School has a real but lightly documented global program. It has seven
sister schools founded between 1989 and 2008, 13 named travel programs for Middle and Upper
School, and Spanish from TK. The public website does not publish the trip prices, deadlines,
selection rules, or participation counts a parent would need, and it offers no global
diploma or certificate. *(Planning note: the Google Site publishes prices, deadlines and
selection rules.)*

sections.text:
- **What exists [Official]:** A "Global Studies" / "Global Education" program with seven
 sister schools in Germany, France, Argentina, Italy, China and South Africa (×2). It lists
 nine Upper School and four Middle School travel programs
 (https://www.charlottelatin.org/about/community-belonging-global-education/global-education).
 The page says "Middle and Upper School students have the chance to explore the world
 through transformative travel experiences." No Lower School student travel is listed.
 Lower School global learning is on campus (Spanish TK–5, Global Partners, Passport
 Program).
- **What's missing:** The public site gives no trip prices, deposits, dates, application
 deadlines, selection method, vendor, or safety/passport guidance. There is no global
 diploma or certificate, and no Round Square membership is published. The detailed trip
 logistics appear to sit on a Global Studies Google Site
 (https://sites.google.com/charlottelatin.org/globalstudies/sister-schools/host-family-faqs).
 That site could not be loaded in this research (tool permission block), so its content is
 unverified, not absent. *(Planning note: it loads; see above.)*
- **Scale:** The only participation figure is secondary. A February 2026 recruiting
 brochure by Carney, Sandoe & Associates says 73 students take part in a domestic or
 international travel program each year
 (https://www.carneysandoe.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Director-of-Community-Belonging-and-Global-Education.pdf, p. 2).
 Against 1,552 enrolled TK–12, that is a small share (PDF's calculation: 73 ÷ 1,552 ≈ 4.7%).
- **The money [Official]:** No trip-specific endowment or named global fund is published.
 The closest is the Plus Fund, financed by the Alumni Endowment (stated value $3.1
 million). Per the school, it pays for costs beyond tuition, explicitly including "travel
 experiences," for families on substantial aid
 (https://www.charlottelatin.org/support/alumni/alumni-giving). Tuition bills include "an
 advance payment of up to $710 for class trips" for grades 5–8 and 12
 (https://www.charlottelatin.org/admissions/tuition-financial-assistance).
- **Bottom line for parents:** Latin is a good fit if you want sister-school exchanges with
 homestays and reciprocal hosting. It is a weaker fit if you want a structured credential
 like Providence Day's Global Studies Diploma or broad, guaranteed participation. Before
 committing, ask for the current trip list with prices and the aid policy in writing.

- **Names and branding [Official]:** The Leading Programs page is titled "Global Studies and
 Travel Opportunities," tagline "LEADING WITH A WORLDWIDE LENS"
 (https://www.charlottelatin.org/leading-programs/global-studies-and-travel-opportunities).
 A parallel page, "Global Education," sits under "Community, Belonging, and Global
 Education" (Global Education page; metadata last published 2026-08-28).
- **Mission language [Official]:** "Global Studies is an integral part of leadership
 development at Latin. Through purposeful coursework, sister school partnerships, and
 international travel, students cultivate the global awareness and cross-cultural
 communication skills essential for leading with empathy and thoughtful decision-making in
 a complex, interconnected world." (global-studies-and-travel-opportunities). The Global
 Education page uses nearly identical wording but "cultural competency skills"; it adds:
 "This work carries out our commitment to community and belonging on a global scale."
- **Director's statement [Official]:** "At its core, Charlotte Latin's Global Studies
 programming seeks to spark curiosity, embrace and elevate different perspectives, foster
 interpersonal connections that transcend borders, and inspire students to advocate for a
 better world for all." — Kelly Willis, Director of Global Studies.
- **Leading Programs framing [Official]:** "The Global Studies program introduces our
 students to new cultures and perspectives, preparing them to live in faraway places and
 to be good citizens in our increasingly diverse communities."
 (https://www.charlottelatin.org/leading-programs).
- **Who runs it — CONFLICT/TRANSITION FLAG:** The program page names "Kelly Willis,
 Director of Global Studies." A February 2026 search brochure [Secondary] recruits a new
 "Director of Community, Belonging, and Global Education", "Start Date: July 2026",
 reporting "to the Associate Head of School", with a "Global Programs Manager" and
 "part-time Belonging and Global Education Coordinators" in each division (Carney Sandoe
 pp. 1, 8–9). The school's ZipRecruiter posting [Secondary]: "starting on July 1, 2026"
 (https://www.ziprecruiter.com/c/CHARLOTTE-LATIN-SCHOOL/Job/Director-of-Community,-Belonging,-and-Global-Education/-in-Charlotte,NC?jid=3021906dd4930874).
 The School Leadership page [Official] (https://www.charlottelatin.org/about/school-leadership,
 last published 2026-08-06) lists "Dr. Teneshia Taylor — Director of Community, Belonging,
 and Global Education." The PDF concludes the program page is out of date.
- **Organization across divisions [Official]:** Upper School programs, Middle School
 programs, Faculty Development, On-Campus Programming (incl. Lower School Passport and
 Global Partners programs).
- **When it started:** No founding date for the Global Studies office is published. The
 earliest dated element is the German sister school "(1989)". The school was "Established
 1970" (Carney Sandoe p. 2).

- **fetched** — page text retrieved 2026-10-13 and the claim read in it.

- **PDF only** — in the deep-research PDF, not yet checked against a page. **Not sufficient
